text: Aífe is an Irish heroine. Several legendary Irish figures bear this name, which means radiant or beautiful. Aífe of Scotland was a great warrior who trained Irish heroes. She was the daughter, sister, or double of the warrior woman Scáthach. The Ulster hero Cúchulainn came to study with Scáthach. He bested Aífe in battle, and she bore his child, Connla. Cúchulainn later unwittingly killed his own son in combat. A second Aífe was the jealous stepmother of the Children of Lir. She took the place of her sister Áeb as wife of Lir. She turned Fionnuala and her brothers into swans for nine hundred years. A third Aífe was transformed into a crane by the jealous Iuchra. The sea god Manannán mac Lir later made the crane bag from her skin.

okr.objective: This article establishes Aífe as the name of several Irish heroines, including a warrior, a stepmother, and a woman turned into a crane.
